text:
mihir: hitting a weird bug in the python SDK streaming client. after a transient 502 and a retry, the resumed stream sometimes repeats a few characters (like "\"ing\" -> "\"inging\"") and the app sees duplicated tokens. repro steps and logs below, any ideas? :eyes:

laura: can you paste the minimal repro and the version of the sdk?

mihir: v0.12.3 (pip). minimal repro: using chat_stream API in asyncio, cancel on timeout, then retry the request. code: ```py
async with RedwoodClient(api_key=KEY) as c:
    async for chunk in c.chat.stream(model="xlarge", messages=msgs):
        print(chunk.text, end="")
```
I see duplication only when the previous connection returns a 502 from the gateway and the client does the automatic retry. logs show the last bytes of previous connection included in the new stream.

sam: does this only happen with streaming or also with non-streaming chunked responses?

mihir: only streaming so far. non-streaming retries produce a single response (no duplicates).

laura: sounds like the replay path is resending the last partial fragment because we don't correctly track the stream cursor when a connection dies mid-chunk. SDK historically used a simple idempotency-key for non-streaming requests but streaming needed sequence ids.

olivia: are we using asyncio.CancelledError anywhere that might leave the socket in a half-read state? cancellation + reconnect could cause leftover bytes to be interpreted. also, typing note: our streaming iterator no longer exposes a .resume_after(seq_id) API which would make this unambiguous  we removed it during the async refactor.

sam: small suggestion: when we reconnect, compare the prefix of the new stream with the end of the cached buffer and drop overlapping bytes. crude but effective if we have a deterministic tokenization boundary.

mihir: logs from the client: ```
[2026-03-19T15:02:30Z] stream: read 128 bytes -> "...learn\"
[2026-03-19T15:02:30Z] conn error: 502 Bad Gateway
[2026-03-19T15:02:30Z] retrying stream with idempotency_key=abc123
[2026-03-19T15:02:30Z] stream: read 64 bytes -> "ing\"
```
So the second stream begins with "ing" which used to be part of the first chunk. result printed: "learninging"

laura: that matches our old bug #412 logic. we fixed similar with sync clients by attaching increasing sequence numbers to events, but the async/stream codepath was refactored and lost seq numbers. PR idea: attach a per-stream sequence counter to SSE chunks (or chunk offsets) and make resume ask the server for the next offset instead of replaying from idempotency key start. server change required but can be backwards-compatible (server falls back to idempotency replay if no offset provided).

olivia: typings-wise we should add a StreamResumeToken = NewType("StreamResumeToken", str) so callers can opt-in to storing resume tokens, and expose resume_token on the iterator: `for chunk in stream: print(chunk.text); token = stream.resume_token`. then a `client.chat.stream_resume(token=token)` helper. That makes demos explicit and helps sample apps.

sam: i'm worried about the rollout. if we add offsets and server doesn't know them, we need to ensure the SDK still behaves safely and doesn't duplicate too often. fallback heuristic: if resumed stream's first chunk equals suffix of last seen text, drop the overlap up to N chars (N small, 8) and emit a debug log.

nick: please open a GH issue with stack trace, logs, and minimal repro. assign to @devex and link to server ticket when created. i'll triage tomorrow.

mihir: created https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-python/issues/2135 with logs and the snippet, assigned to devex. thanks. :+1:

dev-bot: ticket sdk-python#2135 created and linked to internal infra ticket INFR-881.

laura: thanks. quick patch I prototyped: add per-chunk seq headers and a small overlap-trim heuristic when seqs are not available. will open a draft PR with tests and a sample app showing resume semantics. mention in changelog that streaming retries may drop up-to-8-char overlaps until server-offered offsets land.

olivia: can we also add an integration test in sample-apps/streaming-resume that simulates connection drop and asserts no duplication? that's a good onboarding example for folks integrating the stream API.

sam: +1. also add a note in docs about cancellation and proper use of stream.resume_token so users don't accidentally double-process tokens after manual reconnects.

mihir: awesome  eager to try the draft. thanks all.
